topic: Rajshahi University provost relieved after journalist attack
headline_marked: [[RU provost removed]] after attack on journalists; investigation committee formed, report due in 3 days
headline: RU provost removed after attack on journalists; investigation committee formed, report due in 3 days
summary: Rajshahi University's provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall has been immediately relieved of duties following an attack on journalists and students. An investigation committee has been formed, tasked to submit its report within three working days.
details: Rajshahi University (RU) administration has immediately relieved Professor Mahbubur Rahman, provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall, from his duties. This decision follows an attack on journalists and students at the university.

The university has also formed an investigation committee, which is instructed to submit its report within three working days. Those identified as guilty will face temporary expulsion, and their names will be included in the chargesheet filed in the case.

The incident occurred on Sunday night in front of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall, where at least 10 individuals, including four journalists, were injured. Eyewitnesses and injured journalists allege that activists of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) were involved in the assault.

University administration officials held discussions with student and journalist representatives late Monday night, addressing six demands from the protestors. Vice-Chancellor Professor Farid Uddin Islam announced the decisions after over two hours of talks.

The VC stated that individuals found guilty would be temporarily expelled, and a syndicate meeting would be called within 15 days for permanent expulsion. Those without student status will have their certificates cancelled and be banned from campus.

Journalist organizations at RU have declared a boycott of all university administration programs until the investigation report is submitted and visible, effective measures are taken against those involved. They will also monitor the implementation of promises.

Earlier, the central JCD expelled three leaders and issued show-cause notices to six others for violating discipline in connection with the incident. The university's initial case did not name specific individuals, leading to protests by journalists and students who briefly blockaded administrative officials.

topic: ACC files new case against Far East ex-chairman and 7 others
headline_marked: [[ACC files new case against 7]] including ex-Far East Life chairman over BDT 70.20 crore embezzlement
headline: ACC files new case against 7 including ex-Far East Life chairman over BDT 70.20 crore embezzlement
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has accused former Far East Life Insurance chairman Md Nazrul Islam and six others of embezzling approximately BDT 70.20 crore through fraudulent land development schemes and misusing policyholder funds.
details: Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has filed a new case against former Far East Islami Life Insurance Company Limited chairman Md Nazrul Islam and six others. The charges involve abuse of power, fraud, and forgery, leading to the embezzlement of approximately BDT 70.20 crore from the company.

The case was filed by ACC's Deputy Assistant Director Md Sajib Ahmed at the Integrated District Office Dhaka-1 on October 1. The public relations officer of Far East Islami Life Insurance Company Limited, Prashanta Subhash Chandra, confirmed this information on Monday.

The accused include former CEO Md Hemayet Ullah, former Chief Engineer Amir Mohammad Ibrahim, former Company Secretary Syed Abdul Aziz, former Deputy Managing Director Mohammad Alamgir Kabir, former Senior Executive Vice President Sheikh Abdur Razzak, and former Head of Internal Audit Md Kamal Hossain Hawladar.

According to the ACC's First Information Report (FIR), the defendants colluded to create fake bills and vouchers for land and land development work. They allegedly used decisions from the company's Investment and Real Estate Development Sub-Committee (IDRC) meetings to facilitate these fraudulent transactions.

Funds were embezzled by withdrawing money through checks and cash against these fabricated bills. ACC documents show that the IDRC's 276th meeting on June 5, 2018, recommended approving a provisional budget of BDT 100 crore for land and land development.

However, investigations revealed that actual work was not performed, and fake bills and vouchers were created. The FIR states that BDT 69.199 million was withdrawn through 15 checks based on these fraudulent claims.

Additionally, there are allegations that policyholders' due payments were not properly settled after their insurance policies matured. Instead, checks were issued to various individuals and organizations, and cash was withdrawn. The case has been filed under relevant sections of the law.
